issues.legal_issue: A separately owned coke plant that does not extract coal is not a coal mine, and its operator is not an employer under the provident fund scheme, merely because the plant is adjacent to or situated on land associated with a coal mine.
material_facts: The operator owned a coke plant that had been transferred to him separately from the collieries and coal mine.
The operator leased the land on which the plant stood from the company that owned the coal mine; the plant was adjacent to the mine and situated on surface land forming part of the coalfield.
The operator did not excavate coal or carry on operations to obtain coal; the plant manufactured hard coke and other by-products.
The operator was prosecuted for failing to pay employer and employee provident fund contributions and submit returns under the scheme.
issues.conclusion: The operator was not the owner of a coal mine and was not liable as an employer under the scheme on these facts. The appeal was dismissed and the acquittal upheld.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 2(e) of the Coal Mines Provident Fund and Bonus Schemes Act, 1948, an employer is the owner of a coal mine. By section 8 of the General Clauses Act, the reference to the definition of owner in the repealed Indian Mines Act, 1923, is read with the corresponding definition in section 2(l) of the Mines Act, 1952; see State of Uttar Pradesh v. M.P. Singh. Section 2(b) of the 1952 Act defines a coal mine by reference to excavation for obtaining coal and includes associated works, machinery, tramways and sidings. The word “or” before “belonging to a coal mine” is read as “and,” so those subsidiary things are included only when they appertain to and belong to the mine, in the sense of being under the same ownership. Mere adjacency or location on coalfield land does not suffice.

rule.if: scheme_employer_prosecution and plant_separately_owned_from_mine and operator_does_not_extract_coal and plant_adjacent_to_or_on_mine_land

predicates.scheme_employer_prosecution: The proceeding alleges that a person failed to meet scheme obligations on the ground that the person was an employer of a coal mine.
predicates.plant_separately_owned_from_mine: One person owns the plant while another person owns the coal mine.
predicates.operator_does_not_extract_coal: The plant operator does not excavate coal or carry on operations to obtain coal.
predicates.plant_adjacent_to_or_on_mine_land: The plant is adjacent to the mine or stands on land associated with the mine.

issues.definition: When a scheme-employer prosecution concerns a separately owned plant whose operator does not extract coal, adjacency to or location on mine-associated land alone does not make that operator a mine owner or scheme employer.

issues.legal_issue: A later amendment may be used to clarify an earlier ambiguous statutory definition, and may confirm rather than change the earlier law.
material_facts: The 1965 amendment replaced the earlier definition of a coal mine with a more detailed definition.
The amended definition continued to describe relevant works and equipment as being in or adjacent to and belonging to a coal mine.
The Court considered the amendment when interpreting the earlier definition applicable to the dispute.
issues.conclusion: The amendment was intended to fix the proper interpretation of the earlier definition, not to change the law on the ownership requirement.
issues.legal_principle: Where an earlier enactment is obscure, ambiguous, or capable of more than one interpretation, subsequent legislation may be considered in identifying its proper meaning. The Court relied on Ormond Investment Co. Ltd. v. Betts, [1928] A.C. 143, at 166, and treated the 1965 amendment’s continued ownership language as confirming the interpretation of the earlier definition.

predicates.earlier_definition_is_ambiguous: The earlier statutory definition is obscure, ambiguous, or capable of more than one interpretation.
predicates.later_amendment_addresses_same_definitio: A later enactment replaces or revises the same statutory definition.
predicates.later_amendment_retains_ownership_link: The later enactment continues to link included works or equipment to the mine by requiring that they belong to it.

issues.definition: When an ambiguous earlier definition is revised by a later enactment that retains its ownership link, the later enactment may confirm the earlier meaning without changing the law.
